title: Two settings for one speaker
bodyMd:
A survey asked residents which language they used most often at home. Ten years later, a second survey asked which language they used most often at work. The proportion naming the regional language was much lower in the second survey. A newspaper described this as a rapid decline in the language's use. A sociolinguist cautioned that the two questions measured different settings. A person could use the regional language with family and another language with colleagues on the same day.

To investigate change over time, the sociolinguist proposed repeating both questions with comparable samples in a later survey and locating any earlier records that distinguished the two settings. She did not rule out a real decline. Her point was that a difference between settings could not automatically be treated as a difference between years.
